final_proof:
There are two type errors in the explanatory bullets of the statement. If L: \mathbf D \to \mathbf C, then the opposite functor is L^{\mathrm{op}}:\mathbf D^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf C^{\mathrm{op}}, not a functor from \mathbf C^{\mathrm{op}} to \mathbf D^{\mathrm{op}}. Also, the ordinary hom bifunctor of \mathbf C has type \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(-,-):\mathbf C^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathbf C\to\mathbf{Set}, not \mathbf D^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathbf C\to\mathbf{Set}. Thus the literal types printed in those bullets do not define the asserted composite. With these evident corrections, the claimed identity is well-typed and true, as follows.

Write H=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(-,-):\mathbf C^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathbf C\to\mathbf{Set}. Local smallness of \mathbf C ensures that every value of H is a set. The product functor P=L^{\mathrm{op}}\times\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C} has type
\[
P:\mathbf D^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathbf C\longrightarrow\mathbf C^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathbf C.
\]
For an object (d,c), it is given by P(d,c)=(Ld,c). Consequently,
\[
(H\circ P)(d,c)=H(Ld,c)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(Ld,c).
\]
This is exactly the object assignment of the hom bifunctor with left functor L.

It remains to compare the morphism assignments. Let (\alpha,f):(d,c)\to(d',c') be a morphism in \mathbf D^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathbf C. Thus f:c\to c' is a morphism of \mathbf C, while \alpha:d\to d' in \mathbf D^{\mathrm{op}} corresponds to a morphism u:d'\to d in \mathbf D. The morphism L^{\mathrm{op}}(\alpha):Ld\to Ld' in \mathbf C^{\mathrm{op}} corresponds to L(u):Ld'\to Ld in \mathbf C. By the definition of the hom bifunctor, H sends the pair (L^{\mathrm{op}}(\alpha),f) to the function
\[
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(Ld,c)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(Ld',c'),\qquad h\longmapsto f\circ h\circ L(u).
\]
But this is precisely the morphism assignment in the definition of \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(L-,-). Hence the two functors agree on every object and every morphism. Therefore, with the corrected types,
\[
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(L-,-)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(-,-)\circ\bigl(L^{\mathrm{op}}\times\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}\bigr)
\]
as functors \mathbf D^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathbf C\to\mathbf{Set}.
